title: Heat capacity of aqueous sodium chloride from 320 to 600 K measured with a new flow calorimeter
experimental_method: New differential flow heat-capacity calorimeter (thermistor bridge, shunt-controlled heater powers), heat-loss factor f from a physical calibration by flow bleeding; NaCl(aq) 0.1 to 3.0 mol/kg, 320 to 603 K at 17.7 MPa, plus 320.55 K / 1.0 MPa and 572.14 K / 10 MPa.
uncertainties_stated: Ps/Pw readable to +/-0.0001; repeatability a little better than 1 per cent of (Ps/Pw - 1); accuracy about 1 per cent at 320 K, about 5 per cent of (Ps/Pw - 1) at 600 K (heat-loss correction up to 14 per cent at 603 K); pressures +/-0.17 MPa; thermometer 0.11 K at 323 K to 0.36 K at 573 K; molalities +/-0.1 per cent.
quality_remarks: Physical calibration not reproducible to better than 5 per cent at high T; correction factor at 600 K larger than expected. Fit residual largest (7 per cent) at 497.73 K, 0.0996 mol/kg. Internal checks (Cp,phi recomputed from cp,s/cp,w with eq (4) and the water cp of Table 1): Table 2 agrees to within 0.2 J/(K mol) at all T up to 572.14 K, but at 603.39 K the printed Cp,phi values imply a water cp of about 6.07 J/(g K) instead of the 6447 J/(K kg) printed in Table 1 for 603.4 K (Cp,phi would be 35 to 131 J/(K mol) more negative with 6.447); the cp ratios themselves are consistent with Ps/Pw and f = 1.14. Table 3: printed cp,s/cp,w 0.07330 (572.14 K, 3.0000 mol/kg) is a misprint for 0.70330; printed ratio 0.97925 (572.14 K, 0.0996 mol/kg) lacks the density division (Cp,phi corresponds to 0.97534). At 320.55 K / 1.0 MPa the implied water cp scatters (4.137 to 4.148, 3.958 at 3 mol/kg). All values kept as printed. Temperatures are the initial (inlet) temperatures; cell temperature rise (2.0 +/- 0.2) K. Temperature scale not stated.
